title: Digit-Force-Calibration: force-sensing resistor on the rear of a DIGIT optical sensor
rights: Publicly readable. The pinned tree has no license file. Preserve attribution and distribute links, independently written code, and aggregate statistics only.
evidence_level: Both original force calibration CSVs, both published inverse-lookup curves, acquisition program and calibration notebook inspected.
protocol: A force-sensing resistor is mounted behind a DIGIT sensor. The operator presses centrally onto a tared scale, stabilizes the target load, starts the capture, and can keep or redo the trial. The Pico logs a u16 ADC and voltage computed with a 3.3 V reference for approximately three seconds per trial. Both sensors use three trials per target, 19 scale targets from 25 to 1500 g. The same nominal force applies to every row in each trial.
counterexample: The analysis notebook deliberately drops low-load and non-monotonic calibration knots and inserts (0 N, 0 V). On the published raw calibration records, 162/3299 and 287/3363 readings exceed the respective maximum lookup voltage. No digital reading equals ADC code 65535. The piecewise-linear inverse with constant endpoint extrapolation reaches its maximum output long before the digital input rail. The physical resistor, electronics or manipulator may still have other limitations.
method: Independently decode all raw CSV fields. Use 9.81 m/s² and source target mass as reference. Interpolate with endpoint clamping on each published curve and repeat using the other sensor curve. Report raw ADC extrema, coverage outside the calibrated positive knots and mean-square discrepancies by source target and sensor. Rows in the two calibration datasets are not independent holdout experiments.
limits: A scale target is a manually stabilized per-trial reference. No synchronized scale time series or independent force tracking is available.
The sensor measures scalar load at the tactile interface. Normal force versus voltage cannot validate wrist moment, motor-torque saturation or assembly success.
The two files identify different sensors. The named DIGIT 2020 RA-L paper (10.1109/LRA.2020.2977257) is a hardware-platform citation, not the source of these later FSR records.
